topic: What your body does while you sleep
hook: Your body does this every single night

slides.title: Your brain cleans itself
slides.body: During deep sleep, more cerebrospinal fluid flows through your brain and helps wash away waste that builds up during the day.

slides.title: You get taller
slides.body: At night the discs in your spine rehydrate. In the morning you are about one centimeter taller than in the evening.

slides.title: Your muscles switch off
slides.body: During REM sleep your body blocks almost all voluntary muscles, so you don't act out your dreams.

slides.title: Hormones get to work
slides.body: Much of your growth hormone is released during deep sleep. It helps repair tissues and muscles.

slides.title: Memories get saved
slides.body: Your brain replays what you learned during the day and locks it in. Sleeping after studying really helps.

slides.title: Your temperature drops
slides.body: To fall asleep, your core temperature drops by about half a degree to one degree Celsius. That's why a cool room helps you sleep.

cta: Save this and send it to someone who never sleeps enough
caption: Every night while you sleep, your body is working harder than you think: cleaning your brain, repairing your muscles and saving your memories. Sleep is not wasted time. How many hours do you usually sleep?
